label: --help
stdout:
Reach a kestrel control plane over its operator boundary.

Usage: kestrel [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start         Go from whatever the control plane holds to a Session carrying a Brief, declaring what is missing from what this clone says, and explaining every value before applying it
  apply         Preview and apply one Project, Agent and Trigger declaration document
  organization  Declare and list Organizations
  project       Declare and list Projects
  agent         Declare and list Agents
  credential    Hold, list and forget the Provider Credentials an Organization's Sessions reach a model with
  profile       Declare Subscription Profiles, and hold, list and forget the logins in them
  integration   Register and list Integrations: credentialed connections to external systems
  event         Read the Events recorded for an Organization
  trigger       Declare, inspect, test and control Triggers
  workspace     Read Workspaces
  session       Show, enqueue, list and stop Sessions
  instance      List the Instances held for work that exists nowhere else, and release them
  queue         Read the queue: the limits, one row per occupant with its phase, and one per queued Session
  status        Print the resolved scope, where each value came from, what exists in it, and what to session next
  exit-codes    Print every exit code, what it means, and when a script should branch on it

Options:
      --control-plane <URL>  The control plane's operator boundary [env: KESTREL_CONTROL_PLANE=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:7718]
      --organization <NAME>  The Organization this invocation applies to; without it, a committed .kestrel/organization between the working directory and its repository root, then the only Organization [env: KESTREL_ORGANIZATION=]
